title: Electrochemical conversion of CO₂ plasmas published
excerpt: The Sustainable Energy & Fuels article and an associated Zenodo dataset document research into plasma-based electrochemical carbon dioxide conversion.
body: The article ‘Electrochemical conversion of CO₂ plasmas’ has been published in Sustainable Energy & Fuels, volume 10, issue 9, pages 2327–2343, with an associated dataset available through Zenodo.

The research investigates electrochemical carbon dioxide conversion using non-thermal plasma. It grew from a research portfolio led at the University of Aberdeen that connected electrochemistry, plasma engineering, and inorganic chemistry.
The work was also presented orally at the 248th ECS Meeting in Chicago in October 2025. Full publication details are available in the publications section.

title: CO₂ plasma research presented at the 248th ECS Meeting
excerpt: An oral presentation in Chicago brought the electrochemical CO₂ plasma research to the international electrochemistry community.
body: Electrochemical Conversion of CO₂ Plasmas was presented orally at the 248th ECS Meeting in Chicago, United States, in October 2025.
The presentation formed part of a wider research programme on efficient electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction using non-thermal plasma as an electrolyte.
The subsequent journal article and associated dataset are now included in the publication record.

title: Independent AXA Research Fellowship at Nottingham
excerpt: A €140,000 AXA Research Fund fellowship supports sustainable recovery of critical and rare earth elements from batteries and electronic waste.
body: Haytham Hussein joined the Department of Chemistry at the University of Nottingham as an AXA Research Fellow and principal investigator in September 2024.

The €140,000 AXA Postdoctoral Research Fellowship supports an independent programme on conductive diamond electrochemical cells for the recovery of critical and rare earth elements from batteries and electronic waste.

The programme uses green solvents and bioelectrochemistry to promote circular-economy and sustainable-manufacturing technologies, alongside postgraduate supervision, teaching, and laboratory safety leadership.

title: Invited electrodeposition presentation at ECS Vancouver
excerpt: The 241st ECS Meeting featured an invited presentation on tracking metal electrodeposition from a single atom to a crystalline nanoparticle.
body: An invited presentation at the 241st ECS Meeting in Vancouver, Canada, in June 2022 focused on tracking metal electrodeposition dynamics from nucleation and growth of a single atom to a crystalline nanoparticle.
The associated research combines electrochemistry with advanced microscopy to investigate the earliest stages of metal nucleation and subsequent nanoparticle growth.
The underlying article was published in ACS Nano in 2018 and is included in the publications archive.

title: Diamond materials science at the Royal Society Summer Exhibition
excerpt: ‘Diamond: more than just a gemstone’ introduced advanced materials science to visitors at a major public exhibition in London.
body: Haytham presented ‘Diamond: more than just a gemstone’ at the Royal Society Summer Exhibition in London in July 2016.
The exhibition provided a public setting for discussing the scientific and technological importance of diamond beyond its familiar use as a gemstone.
The exhibition attracted more than 10,000 visitors. This forms part of a broader public-engagement record that also includes the Science Museum’s ‘Science Late’ event in April 2015.
